analysis:
This PR changes only documentation and a changelog fragment: changelog.d/coordinator-reconnect-stall.md (added) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (a drain paragraph near line 444 and a new runtime-constants row near line 1974). No source code was supplied, so none of the behavior the text describes could be verified.

The docs describe two behaviors: (1) a 30 s coordinator handshake deadline (TCP, TLS and WebSocket upgrade) that is cancelled and retried with the reconnect backoff, and (2) a graceful drain that skips the coordinator acknowledgement only when no work is left and the provider has no registered coordinator session. The second bears on the TB-002 and TB-011 lifecycle drain contract and on the T-053 and T-057 availability and stale-authorization concerns.

I found no security regression in the text itself. The drain skip is limited to the no-registered-session case, and a registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. The handshake timeout improves availability against a stalled or hung coordinator connection, which matters for T-057. It does not alter trust or authorization state.

Open integration questions for any pass that sees the code:
- Does CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift apply the timeout only to the connect and upgrade phase, and does it not weaken TLS validation or pinning?
- Is 'no registered coordinator session' determined race-free in performLifecycleDrain? A session that registers just after the check could be dropped without the barrier acknowledgement, which would skip usage settlement. The text says settlement happens only after no unfinished requests remain.
- Does the logout path (ProviderLogout) still require confirmed process exit and not rely on the new skip?

These claims are unverified and belong to code review, not documentation review. Marking deeper review as warranted for the code side only.
